candidateObjectiveEnglish: Name a panel and plywood, recall replace, produce identification/location sentences and recognize a marking instruction.
grammarExplanationEnglish: An imperative uses the base verb without a subject: "Mark the damaged area." "This is a panel" identifies a countable item with a. "This is plywood" names a material without an article. "Where is the panel?" asks for the location of a specific panel.
grammarExplanationFrench: L’impératif emploie le verbe à la forme de base : « Mark the damaged area ». « This is a panel » identifie un objet dénombrable ; « This is plywood » nomme un matériau sans article anglais. « Where is the panel? » demande où se trouve le panneau.
